clue.text: Notice one in tirade incandescent

indicators.note: in tells us the notice and the one go inside the word for a tirade

parts.note: a tirade is a rant
a notice in a newspaper is an ad
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone notices a person ranting, white-hot with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something incandescent glows brightly, shining with light.

clue.text: Polish trick to restrict current in ancient river

indicators.note: to restrict means polish and trick together hold the current symbol between them

parts.note: to polish is to rub
a con is a trick
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Polish trick to stop an electric current in an old river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb polish, capitalised only as the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossed this small river in northern Italy in 49 BC, so it is a river of ancient history.

clue.text: Nothing shown after silent film

indicators.note: shown after says the nought comes after the word for silent

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak, silent
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing appears on screen after a silent movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1941 Disney animated feature about a flying elephant bears this title.

clue.text: Taking it all in having gone round planet?

indicators.note: round says the word for gone goes around the planet word

parts.note: gone means away, absent
an orb is a sphere, such as a planet

explanation.surface: An astronaut, having orbited a planet, takes in all the sights.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge or towel that soaks up liquid is literally taking it all in; the question mark flags the image.

clue.text: Something of a shock — tension initially relieved

indicators.note: initially relieved says the first letter is removed from the word for tension

parts.note: tension means stress or strain

explanation.surface: A shock that brings tension, only for it to be relieved at first.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock of hair is a thick mass of it, so 'Something of a shock' is a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick mop, and a single lock of hair is part of it.

clue.text: Long cushion giving help

definitions.meaning: a long, firm pillow laid across the head of a bed
to help is to prop up or reinforce

explanation.surface: A long cushion offering support.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the long pillow, and the verb meaning to support or strengthen.

clue.text: Corporation to fail — botched entry from board?

parts.note: a corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, a pot belly
to fail is to flop

explanation.surface: A company goes under after a bungled boardroom appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is old British slang for a big stomach; 'board' is a diving board, not a boardroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive in which the swimmer smacks into the water stomach first is a badly executed entry from a diving board.

clue.text: Fools seen within the French city

indicators.note: seen within says the word for fools sits inside the French article

parts.note: LA is French for the (feminine)
fools means tricks, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: Fools turn up inside a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' is a verb, as in 'he has you there'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Tibet, home of the Potala Palace.

clue.text: Watch one's opponent in this event?

definitions.text: Watch one's opponent in this event?

parts.words: Watch one's opponent in this event
parts.note: suggests keeping an eye on a rival, but in this race the rider competes against a watch, the clock

explanation.surface: Advice to keep an eye on a rival during a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' is the timepiece, not the verb: in cycling's race against the clock, the stopwatch is the only opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: In this cycling or running event each competitor races alone against the clock.

clue.text: Reversed role with sailor as pest controller

indicators.note: reversed means role-plus-sailor is read backwards as a whole

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor swaps roles and becomes the ship's pest controller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' turns PARTTAR around as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for catching rodents controls pests, so the definition describes its function.

clue.text: Overwhelming surprise for attractive blonde

definitions.meaning: a shocking piece of news that stuns everyone
slang for a very attractive woman, especially a blonde one

explanation.surface: A stunning blonde arrives unexpectedly and turns heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: shocking news, and the slang term for a strikingly attractive woman, as in 'blonde ...'.

clue.text: Provide student with place and grant

definitions.meaning: a college lets a student in, giving them a place on a course
to grant a point is to concede or confess it

explanation.surface: A university offers a student a place and some funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grant' looks like a student's funding, but here it is the verb meaning concede.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: to let someone in to a college, and to concede that something is true.

clue.text: Almost axe Irish singing group

indicators.note: almost means the word for axe loses its final letter

parts.note: to axe is to chop

explanation.surface: An Irish singing group is nearly cut by budget-cutters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims CHOP to CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, as in a church or concert.

clue.text: One has agents sorting out party mess

indicators.note: sorting out means the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up after a party that left a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of an intelligence network directs a team of secret agents, so this is a description of the job.

clue.text: Name novel bar changed beyond words?

indicators.note: changed means the letters of novel bar are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub with a new name has been transformed past description.
explanation.definitionFit: Communication that does not use words, such as gestures, is literally beyond words; the question mark marks the playful reading.

clue.text: Clothing range with buckles

indicators.note: buckles means the letters of range with bend out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A clothing range sold with buckles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckles' looks like fasteners but is the verb, meaning collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightdresses are garments worn in bed, a category of clothing.

clue.text: Hedonist tense after exam in German city

indicators.note: after says the tense letter follows the rest
in says the exam goes inside the German city

parts.note: Bonn is a city in Germany, once the West German capital
a viva is an oral exam
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: A student feels tense after an exam taken in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is a British oral examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-seeker who lives well, enjoying good food and drink, is a hedonist.

clue.text: From here one may observe second-rate flat

parts.note: B is second class, as in a B grade
flat and limp both mean lacking firmness or energy

explanation.surface: A view is promised from somewhere that turns out to be a dull, second-rate flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the adjective meaning limp.
explanation.definitionFit: Airships and barrage balloons were used as observation platforms, so one might watch from aboard one.

clue.text: Keeping quiet, initiated in slaughter

indicators.note: keeping says the word for initiated holds the quiet sign inside

parts.note: blooded means initiated, given a first experience
SH is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A newcomer is initiated in killing and told to keep quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter and this word are synonyms for killing on a large scale.

clue.text: Some fellahin go to bar

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Egyptian peasant farmers head off to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Fellahin are Egyptian peasant farmers; 'bar' tempts as a pub but is a bar of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal such as gold is cast into a block or bar, the usual form for bullion.

clue.text: Wicked Zulu warriors going over house contents?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means placed above the next part

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: contents means the inside letters of house, without its ends

explanation.surface: Wicked Zulu warriors rampage through a house's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, which is close to wicked or sinful.

clue.text: Number puzzle that's easy

parts.note: a puzzle is a problem to be solved

explanation.surface: A solver dismisses a numbers puzzle as simple.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said when a task presents no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Erasmus dressed as Rubber Man?

indicators.note: dressed means Erasmus is rearranged, like a dressing of letters into new order

explanation.surface: The scholar Erasmus dresses up in a rubber costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' is one who rubs, not latex.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages rubs people's muscles, so he is literally a rubber.

clue.text: Latin poet breaking promise

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of Latin poet are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A classical poet goes back on his word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promise' is a noun here, as in a youngster showing promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Promise in the sense of latent ability to succeed is the same thing as untapped capability.

clue.text: Trained assassin captured by American in Jamaica

indicators.note: captured by says the letters are held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An assassin is captured by an American in Jamaica.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese warrior trained in stealth and covert killing, a classic hired killer.

clue.text: Fruit held up by Burmese military

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fruit shipment is delayed by the Burmese army.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' reads the hidden letters upwards; it also hides them.
explanation.definitionFit: Small green citrus fruits are one kind of fruit.

clue.text: Loves making love?

definitions.meaning: terms of endearment, as a northern English shopkeeper says 'ta, duck'
in cricket a batsman out for no runs has scored zero, and love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about affection and romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a score of zero is a duck; love is zero in tennis, so scoring nothing makes love.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the British endearment 'duck', and cricket's zero scores, which amount to love.

clue.text: Ruthless Conservative line taken without regret

indicators.note: taken without means the two letters sit outside the word for regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A ruthless Tory policy pushed through without any remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless and this word are synonyms for being merciless and pitiless.

clue.text: Round tin Popeye finally dropped in sea

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape

indicators.note: dropped in says a letter is put inside the word for tin

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Popeye

explanation.surface: Popeye's round spinach tin ends up dropped into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped in' puts E, from 'Popeye finally', inside CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea and this word are near-synonyms for a vast body of salt water.

clue.text: Shelter for poor soul has me troubled

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of soul has me are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A troubled soul seeks refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable houses were built to give free lodging to the poor and elderly, a kind of refuge.

clue.text: Man on the lookout when old boy leaves

indicators.note: leaves says the former pupil departs from the word for watchful

parts.note: someone on the lookout is watchful, observant

explanation.surface: A watchman is alert as a former pupil departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb-looking noun: a manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in the old sense is a male attendant or valet who works for a master.

clue.text: All this worker makes going on the horses?

definitions.text: All this worker makes going on the horses?

parts.words: All this worker makes going on the horses
parts.note: reads like a gambler betting all their wages on racing, but describes a craftsman whose products are put on the horses' backs

explanation.surface: A worker gambles every penny he earns on horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on the horses' suggests betting; everything this leatherworker makes literally goes on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The craftsman meant makes the leather seats strapped onto horses' backs for riders.
